content.value_statement: Stitch projects need consistent design guidance across new screens. This skill turns project assets into a clear DESIGN.md source of truth.
actual_capabilities: Guides retrieval of Stitch projects, screens, and metadata through MCP tools.
Uses HTML, screenshots, and designTheme data to infer visual language.
Documents color palettes with names, hex values, and functional roles.
Translates Tailwind and CSS values into plain design descriptions.
Produces a structured DESIGN.md outline for Stitch prompting.
limitations: Requires access to the Stitch MCP Server and the target project.
Depends on available screens, metadata, HTML, and screenshots.
Does not validate whether generated design descriptions match every screen.
Requires user review before sharing project assets or fetched URLs.

use_cases.title: Document A Stitch Project
use_cases.description: Create a reusable DESIGN.md file from an existing Stitch project and screen.

use_cases.title: Translate UI Implementation Details
use_cases.description: Convert Tailwind classes, CSS values, and HTML structure into plain design language.

use_cases.title: Standardize New Screen Prompts
use_cases.description: Give teams a shared visual reference for generating future Stitch screens.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Basic Design Guide
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a known project and screen.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a DESIGN.md guide for this Stitch project. Include theme, colors, typography, components, and layout principles.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One Screen Deeply
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request using a screen as the main source.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Stitch screen in detail. Describe its mood, color roles, typography, component styling, spacing, and reuse rules.

prompt_templates.title: Build A Reusable Prompt Source
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for future screen generation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Synthesize the project assets into a DESIGN.md source of truth that another prompt can use to create consistent new screens.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Multiple Screens
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the available Stitch screens and document shared patterns, exceptions, and recommended design language for future work.

output_examples.input: Analyze a Furniture Collection Stitch project with a Home screen.
output: The guide describes a calm retail interface with generous spacing and soft product imagery.
It names primary action, surface, accent, text, and border colors with functional roles.
It documents buttons, cards, forms, and layout rhythm for future screens.

output_examples.input: Create a design guide from a dashboard screen with HTML and theme metadata.
output: The result explains the dashboard atmosphere, hierarchy, and density.
It translates CSS radius, shadows, and spacing into designer-friendly language.
It gives clear rules for charts, panels, controls, and navigation elements.

best_practices: Provide the project ID or screen ID when available to avoid broad project lookup.
Review fetched HTML and screenshots for sensitive content before analysis.
Validate the generated DESIGN.md against several screens before using it widely.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill on projects you are not authorized to inspect.
Do not accept vague color names without hex values and functional roles.
Do not treat one screen as the full design system when more examples exist.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates DESIGN.md documentation that describes a Stitch project design system in reusable language.

faq.question: Does it require Stitch MCP access?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow expects access to Stitch project, screen, HTML, screenshot, and theme metadata.

faq.question: Can it work from only a screenshot?
faq.answer: It can help from a screenshot, but HTML and theme metadata improve accuracy.

faq.question: Does it generate application code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on design documentation for prompting Stitch consistently.

faq.question: Can teams edit the generated DESIGN.md?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams should review terms, color roles, and component descriptions before reuse.

faq.question: Is project data sent to third parties?
faq.answer: The skill describes fetching Stitch assets for analysis. Users should approve and review any project data used.
